convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load 'CoeffofLine_true' custom indicator and includes external TradeAlgorithms.mqh library. Both require manual Python reimplementation.

derived_values.name: CoeffofLine_true buffer 0 value at SignalBar and SignalBar+1
Value[0] - current signal bar indicator value

other_exits: Long position closed when indicator crosses below zero (Value[1]<0 detected, BuyPosClose=true)
Short position closed when indicator crosses above zero (Value[1]>0 detected, SellPosClose=true)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MM<0 uses absolute value as fixed lot size; MM>0 uses deposit fraction

custom_logic_notes: Entry logic: when Value[1]>0 (indicator on prior bar is positive) AND Value[0]<0 (indicator on signal bar is negative), that is a zero-line crossover upward -> BUY. When Value[1]<0 AND Value[0]>0, zero-line crossunder -> SELL. The SignalBar parameter (default 1) shifts which bar is used for current vs previous value. Exit signals are generated simultaneously: a buy signal also triggers short close, and a sell signal also triggers long close. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh library provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, GlobalVariableDel_, LoadHistory, and CIsNewBar - these must be reimplemented. CoeffofLine_true custom indicator is an SMMA-based coefficient of line indicator; its internal logic must be sourced separately for Python conversion.
external_dependencies: CoeffofLine_true custom indicator (.mq5 source needed for Python reimplementation)
python_conversion_notes: Two main reimplementation tasks: (1) CoeffofLine_true indicator - SMMA(period=5) based, outputs values crossing zero for trend direction; need to locate and port the indicator source code. (2) TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions - position open/close with fixed SL/TP, deposit-fraction sizing (MM negative=lot size, positive=deposit fraction), deviation check, new-bar detection. Entry is zero-line crossover on CoeffofLine_true: buy when crosses above zero, sell when crosses below zero. SignalBar=1 means signals are evaluated on the previous closed bar, so backtest should use bar[1] close price as fill assumption.
